question: Why is Apache Cassandra described as a masterless, shared-nothing architecture?
category: Why is Apache Cassandra described as a masterless, shared-nothing architecture?

options.text: Every node in the cluster plays an identical role; any node can coordinate any read or write request without a single point of failure.
$R + W > N$, where $R$ is Read Consistency, $W$ is Write Consistency, and $N$ is Replication Factor.
Partition Key determines which physical node in the token ring stores the row; Clustering Key determines the on-disk sorting order within that partition.
Last-Write-Wins (LWW) based on microsecond client-side timestamps.

explanation: Every node in the cluster plays an identical role; any node can coordinate any read or write request without a single point of failure.
